seed: New Layer via Copy used to make its new layer out of every layer flattened together the moment a marquee was up, even with a layer picked, so the photo underneath came along baked in. The walk builds a two layer picture, picks the top layer, drags a marquee across its edge, and presses Command J: the new layer should hold that layer's pixels alone and be named after it. Then it checks the other two ways in: nothing picked still promotes everything inside the marquee, and no marquee still duplicates the picked layer.

steps.note: a photo across the whole canvas with a rectangle drawn on top of it, and the rectangle is picked
THE SETUP: the marquee crosses the rectangle's bottom right corner and carries on over bare photo, and the rectangle is still the picked layer

THE TEST: Command J made a new layer out of the RECTANGLE's corner alone, trimmed to it (200 by 150, the part of the rectangle the marquee covers), named the way duplicating that layer names it, and the marquee has cleared
THE PROOF: dragged clear of where it came from, the new layer is a piece of the rectangle and nothing else. Before this fix it was a slab of the photo with the rectangle's corner in it
THE TEST: a marquee that lands entirely off the picked layer makes NOTHING and beeps, the same honest refusal Command C gives, instead of stacking an empty layer
THE TEST: with nothing picked there is nothing to prefer, so Command J still promotes everything inside the marquee, photo and all, at the size the marquee was drawn
THE TEST: with no marquee up, Command J still duplicates the picked layer, exactly as it did before
